figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Function of MDRs in PoTeMs biosynthesis and the apo structure of OX4. (a) OX4 (Lysobacter enzymogenes C3, GenBank: EF028635.2)
catalyzes the reductive cyclization to form the third 6-membered ring in 1a. (b) OX4 reduces 2 to produce 2a. (c) IkaC (Streptomyces sp. ZJ306,
GenBank: KF954512.1) and CftD (Kitasatospora sp. S023, GenBank: MT419890.1) catalyze the reductive cyclization to form the third 5-membered
ring in 3a. (d) Overall structure of the OX4 dimer (monomer A in wheat, monomer B in palecyan). (e) Secondary structure and domain organization
of the OX4 monomer, with the nucleotide-binding domain in lightblue and the catalytic-binding domain in palegreen.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Substrate recognition by OX4. (a) Superposition of three OX4-NADP+-substrate complexes: OX4-NADP+-1 (white), OX4-NADP+-1a
(wheat), OX4-NADP+-2 (cyan). Substrates and cofactors bind at the interface of the two domains and are shown in stick format. (b) Close-up view of
OX4 residues interacting with 3-deOH ATC (1, yellow), with substrate density shown as a blue mesh and hydrogen bonds indicated by black dashed
lines. (c) In vitro activity assay of OX4 with selected mutations. Bars represent the mean of n = 3 independent experiments, with activities normalized to
protein concentration. (d) Reactions catalyzed by OX4, its W260-related mutants, and CftD W261A mutant, respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Substrate stereospecificity of OX4. (a) Close-up view of OX4
residues interacting with 3-deOH ATB (2, cyan), with the substrate
density displayed as a blue mesh and hydrogen bonds represented by
black dashed lines. (b) Conformational differences between substrates
1 (yellow) and 2 (cyan) within the OX4 active site. The distance
between C11 and C22 in substrates 1 and 2, as well as the hydrogen
bond between the C7-carbonyl oxygen and W2, are indicated by black
dashed lines.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Substrate tolerance of OX4. (a) Cyclization reaction catalyzed by OX4/PtmC (Streptomyces pactum SCSIO 02999, GenBank: KU569222.1)
and CftD/IkaC. (b) In vitro assays of OX4, CftD, and CftD291−300 with 1 or 3, respectively. (c) Sliced-surface view showing distinct conformations of 1,
2, and 3 in the OX4 substrate-binding site. Differences in the ornithine moiety are highlighted with a dashed red box. (d) Structural comparison
between the apo forms of OX4 (wheat) and CftD (pale green). (e) Superimposition of the OX4-NADP+-1 structure with the apo-CftD structure,
highlighting conformational changes in three loops. Substrate 1 in OX4 is shown as a yellow stick.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Proposed mechanism for the OX4-catalyzed reaction. Dashed lines represent hydrogen bonding interactions. (a) Biosynthesis of 1a. OX4
reduces 1 to form enolate intermediate I, which cyclizes to form intermediate II, followed by tautomerization to produce 1a. (b) Biosynthesis of 1b.
The OX4 W260F mutant reduced 1 to form enol intermediate III, followed by tautomerization to generate 1b. The C1-carbonyl oxygen of 1 is
protonated by the water molecule W1, which engages in hydrogen bonding with the main-chain carbonyl oxygen of residue Y50.
